title.en: Compound statements and connectives: and, or

title.en: And, or, and their truth tables

body.en: A *compound* statement is built from simple statements with connectives. p ∧ q ("p and q") is true only if both p and q are true. p ∨ q ("p or q", inclusive) is true if at least one is true; it is false only when both are false. Exclusive or is true when exactly one is true. De Morgan's laws: $\sim(p \wedge q) \equiv \sim p \vee \sim q$ and $\sim(p \vee q) \equiv \sim p \wedge \sim q$.

points.en: p ∨ q: at least one true
not(and) = or of nots; not(or) = and of nots

problem.en: p: 3 is a factor of 12. q: 3 is a factor of 14. Find the truth values of p ∧ q, p ∨ q and ~(p ∧ q), and write ~(p ∧ q) in words.

steps.en: p is true (12 = 3 × 4); q is false.
p ∧ q is false; p ∨ q is true; ~(p ∧ q) is true.
By De Morgan, ~(p ∧ q): 3 is not a factor of 12 or 3 is not a factor of 14.
